name: JSW Energy Ltd.
business_summary: JSW Group's power arm: 15.1 GW installed (61% renewable; thermal Ratnagiri, Vijayanagar, Nandyal, KSK Mahanadi, Maruti; hydro Karcham Wangtoo, Baspa, Kutehr, Tidong; wind and solar), 15.3 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 30 GW target by 2030, plus integrated supply chain (Toshiba JSW turbines, GE Power India boilers, wind blades). Q2 FY27: revenue Rs 6,658 cr (+24%), EBITDA Rs 3,907 cr (+23%), PAT Rs 1,141 cr (+38%; attributable Rs 1,056 cr, +50%); net generation 17.5 bn units (+17%); net debt Rs 65,576 cr (5.55x TTM EBITDA); debt cost 8.28%. FY27 capex ~Rs 20,000 cr. Promoters 66.5%, mcap Rs 95.5k cr, P/E 40.6.

revenue_mix.geography: India (HP, Karnataka, TN, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra)

exposures.mechanism: Highest leverage in the batch: net debt Rs 65,576 cr (operational 58,410 + CWIP 7,166), 5.55x TTM EBITDA; EV/MCap ~1.7 (mcap Rs 95.5k cr). CFO (28 Oct): ~25% of term debt fixed, ~75% floating of which ~90% is linked to lenders' MCLR (lags repo). Assume 55% of the repo move passes within 12m: Rs 65.6k cr x 75% x 25bp x 55% = Rs 68 cr/yr = -2.4% of TTM PAT (Rs 2.8k cr) -> ~-0.8% of mcap capitalised at 10x less PPA indexation; plus equity-risk repricing => -3.0. Debt cost fell 51bp YoY to 8.28% so there is refinancing cushion.

evidence.note: CFO Prabhakaran: ~25% of term debt fixed; ~90% of floating linked to MCLR; debt cost 8.28% vs 8.79% a year ago
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: P/E 40.6, P/B 2.6; 61% of capacity renewable on 25-yr PPAs, thermal PPAs with 14-25 yr remaining life. Equity duration ~14 on ~10% cost of equity: +25bp => -3.5% unadjusted; JSW Steel shareholding (market value) and cash Rs 15.7k cr dampen => -2.5.

evidence.note: Mcap Rs 95,460 cr, P/E 40.6, ROE 7.5%
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: FY27 capex ~Rs 20,000 cr against ~Rs 6,500 cr accruals and Rs 7,150 cr (fund raise + JSW Steel share sales) = equity visibility Rs 13,150 cr; the ~Rs 7k cr gap plus Rs 15k cr of refinancing as projects commission must be funded in bond/loan markets. +50bp on Rs 22k cr = Rs 110 cr/yr = -3.9% of PAT x 0.5 persistence x EV/MCap 1.7 ... => -2.5. ICRA/India Ratings affirmed AA stable.

evidence.note: Capex ~Rs 20,000 cr FY27; accruals ~Rs 6,500 cr; ICRA and India Ratings affirmed AA/Stable

exposures.mechanism: Merchant realisation Rs 6.9/unit (20% above Rs 5.7 DAM average) after bilateral contracts; merchant/short-term sales ~12% of volume (estimate; 15.3 GW of PPA signed; Maruti adds 64 MW merchant). +15% spot => +1.8% revenue at ~100% drop-through = +3.1% EBITDA (margin 58%) x EV/MCap 1.7 x persistence 0.4 => +2.1; haircut for fixed-price conversions => +1.8.

evidence.note: Merchant realisation ~Rs 6.9/unit vs DAM Rs 5.7/unit in Q2 FY27; 96 plants critical on coal stock in Oct
Under-construction PPA signed 15,348 MW; pipeline with LoA 2,761 MW

exposures.mechanism: Q2 net generation +17% YoY to 17.5 bn units on capacity + demand (power demand +11.1% in Q2, Oct MTD +21%); thermal PLF and merchant volumes rise; most PPAs are capacity-based so only ~25% of the incremental volume converts. +3pp demand => EBITDA +1.0% x 1.7 x 0.7 => +1.2.

evidence.note: Power demand +11.1% in Q2, Oct-to-date +21.2%; net generation +17% to 17.5 bn units

exposures.mechanism: Hydro is ~20% of generation (3,421 MU in Q2, +13%: Karcham Wangtoo, Baspa, Kutehr, Tidong) with some energy-linked revenue; good monsoon raises hydro (+) but lowers thermal/merchant demand and prices (-). Net small positive: +10% => hydro +8% of 20% = +1.6% of generation, EBITDA +1.0%; thermal demand loss -0.7% => +0.3 equity at EV/MCap 1.7 x persistence 0.25.

evidence.note: Hydro generation 3,421 MU (+13%) despite All-India hydro -15% and monsoon ~13% below normal

exposures.mechanism: Insulated: shifted to domestic coal and 'job-work' arrangements at imported-coal plants (Ratnagiri/Maruti linkage), so seaborne API4 (~US$115/t in Q2, +28% YoY) mostly hits others; merchant prices and Salboni/KSK optionality benefit modestly. Pack empirical +1.90 (t +0.9) agrees in sign. +15% => +0.4.

evidence.note: Sharad Mahendra: transition to domestic coal and job-work at imported plants shields from fuel-price volatility; API4 ~US$115/t
Pack empirical F_COAL_INTL +1.90, t +0.9

exposures.mechanism: Domestic coal under SHAKTI/FSA is the main thermal fuel (Maruti fully via SECL FSA); pass-through exists under most PPAs but KSK (1,800 MW, PPA with MP etc.) and merchant volume are exposed. +10% => unrecovered ~15% of Rs 2k cr/qtr fuel x ... => -1.0% EBITDA x 1.7 x 0.35 => -0.6.

evidence.note: Maruti plant fully domestically fuelled via long-term FSA with SECL and SHAKTI linkage

exposures.mechanism: 3 GW RE commissioning target FY27 (1.4 GW done), 30 GW by 2030, curtailment 4.8% of generation (59 cr revenue in Q2) with 60% moving from temporary to permanent GNA by end-Q3. Stronger support (GNA, ISTS, storage VGF) removes curtailment (-2% revenue) and lifts pipeline: +3.5.

evidence.note: Curtailment ~4.8% of generation in H1; ~225 MU in Q2 costing Rs 59 cr; permanent GNA by end Q3
